title: Watch the platform: the backup status and the dashboard of companies for the operator; everyone else refused (read-only)
description: The platform administrator reads the backup status (200, 'configured' and the list of jobs) and the list of companies that the platform dashboard shows. A company administrator and a storekeeper are refused the backup status with the fixed 403 ; a caller without a sign-in gets 401. Read-only: nothing is created, there is no cleanup and no residue; the fixture tenant is not needed. UNMATCHED ADDRESSES are not probed: the static check of the runner cannot route-match an address that no route has, and the behaviour (the fixed 403 for a non-operator, the router's 404 for the operator) is covered by test/letflow/routers/platform_status_test.exs, event_retention_test.exs and platform_problem_reports_test.exs. GAP, a RUNNER limit and not a product gap: the three anonymous routes of the entry (GET /health, GET /ready, GET /metrics) are outside /api/, and the runner's static check requires every path to start with /api/; /health is read by the runner's own preflight (the build sha, at the start and at the end of every run) but is not a step with an expectation, and /ready and /metrics (no tenant label in the text) have no step. Runner task wanted: a step kind (or a rule) that allows the anonymous actor to call /health, /ready and /metrics. Screens (the health dashboard and the metrics page) are screen-only and are not run here.

steps.says: The operator reads the backup status: 200 with the flag 'configured' and the list of jobs (each with its age). The list may be empty when no backup is configured on QA; that is an answer, not a failure. T-3107: the list may be empty, so the step asserts that the list is THERE (`present`), not that it holds a job.

steps.positional_ok: any row of the list will do: the step only needs one existing row and uses the same row for every field it reads
steps.says: The platform dashboard reads the list of companies: 200 and at least the platform company itself.
A company administrator is refused the backup status with the fixed 403.
A storekeeper is refused it too.
Without a sign-in the backup status is refused: 401.
